summary: The XPeng X9 is a large seven-seat electric people mover sold in two grades, a $89,900 FWD Standard Range and a $109,900 AWD Performance, pitched at the Kia Carnival, Denza D9 and Zeekr 009. Australian reviewers rate it highly for space, luxury and comfort: CarExpert calls the third row surprisingly usable and the four-wheel steering makes it feel smaller than it is. The knocks are software gremlins (a test car that shut down and wouldn't select a gear), an intrusive lane-keeping system, a ride that can wallow in its softest mode, and a $20,000 jump to the AWD grade.
pros: 721 L boot with all seven seats in use and up to 2,554 L with the second and third rows folded, plus an adult-usable, heated third row
Fast 800V charging: up to 537 kW (Standard Range) and 542 kW (AWD), a claimed 10-80% in 12 minutes
Long WLTP range for the class: 535 km (94.8 kWh LFP) and 580 km (110 kWh NCM) on 20-inch wheels
Four-wheel steering gives a 5.4 m turning circle, and CarExpert says it makes the X9 feel smaller than it is
7-year unlimited-km warranty for private buyers, with the battery and drive motor covered for 8 years/160,000 km
cons: Software and key gremlins: CarExpert's test car shut down mid-test and would not engage a gear until the NFC card was used
Lane-keeping assist is intrusive enough that CarExpert switched it off on every drive
The FWD Standard Range is not approved for towing; only the AWD Performance takes a tow bar (1,500 kg braked)
The AWD Performance costs $20,000 more and sits above the $91,661 luxury car tax threshold, while the Standard Range sits just under it
No spare wheel, no capped-price servicing, and connected services become a paid plan after one year
